MINUTES
  REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  JANUARY 23, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR SCHMITZ at 7:03 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG
  CHAIR SCHMITZ led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Brtis, Ciarolla, Griggs, Nilsen, Shinn, Silvano,
  Robinson, Harik, and Schmitz
  Committee Members Absent:  Martin and Schachter
  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 24, 2022
  MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN to:
  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE OCTOBER 24, 2022,
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.
5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
  NONE.
6.  STAFF ITEMS
A.  REQUEST FROM PORTUGUESE BEND HORSE SHOW FOR ARENA
  RENOVATIONS

  CHAIR SCHMITZ explained that the two arena renovations requests would be
  discussed one at a time.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a verbal overview of the first
  Portuguese Bend National Horse Show (PBNHS) request per written report. He
  clarified that that the show had been held since 1958.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 23, 2023
  1
   MEMBER NILSON asked who would pay the cost of the renovation.
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that had not yet been determined.
  MEMBER GRIGGS asked how much revenue the City receives from the PBNHS.
  Supervisor Pinuelas responded that the City received $6,700 the previous year.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the revenue received was for the PBNHS facility
  rental fees in response to MEMBER NILSON.
  MEMBER GRIGGS asked if the new footing would work for both a Western rider
  and an English rider. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that staff is still
  researching the footing, but it seems to be a GGT blend with less fabric.
  MEMBER SHINN inquired about the previous instance when the City changed out
  the footing and asked where the footing that was removed was placed.
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that it was changed in in 2012 and then
  changed back in 2013, stating that some was utilized in other City arenas and that
  the rest was sold to local stables.
  MEMBER SHINN asked if the existing Western Blend footing was needed or if the
  previous type of footing could be put back in since that the western shows are not
  returning and if the arena needed to remain a western arena. Superintendent
  Goldsmith responded that staff was attempting to satisfy the needs of everyone.
  MEMBER GRIGGS stated that she sees people trying to do pole bending and such
  and thinks they would like to have an arena where they can continue to do so.
  MEMBER HARIK inquired about the maintenance cost of the new blend versus
  sand. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that more information is needed
  regarding the blend but that it seems like typical maintenance would be needed
  and that staff would be capable of maintaining it.
  MEMBER SILVANO asked when staff anticipated needing to redo the footing in
  Arena 2. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that there are no plans to redo the
  footing but stated sand needs to be added to the arena, which is regular
  maintenance.
  CHAIR SCHMITZ explained the process for questions and comments and invited
  the representatives from PBNHS to speak.
  Carole Rowe, 2023 PBNHS Chair, shared information about the show which
  benefits the Peninsula Committee Children’s Hospital (PCCH). She explained that
  the PBNHS features an array of hunter jumper events and medal finals which are
  sanctioned and assigned to PCCH by the Pacific Coast Horse Show Association
  (PCHA). Ms. Rowe stated that there has been a decrease in participation as a
  result of the footing in the rings and that the main issue they would like to pursue
  is the replacement of the footing in Arena 2. She added that PCCH is hoping the
  City can use any available funds to complete the project. Ms. Rowe stated that
  funds raised for PCCH are limited to funding programs specific to its mission.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 23, 2023
  2
   Ms. Rowe affirmed that the request is to install the partial GGT footing in response
  to CHAIR SCHMITZ. Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis asked if PBNHS is
  requesting a permanent installation of the footing. Ms. Rowe responded that that
  permanent installation is the preference, but that they are open to an alternative if
  there is another economical solution.
  Devon Gibson, PBNHS representative, stated their biggest need is to make Arena
  2 usable for the hunters and jumpers who attend to show. She shared that the
  Western Blend footing would be ideal and most beneficial to Western and English
  riding, and Gymkhana and that she will be investigating further. Ms. Gibson stated
  that she believes this change will keep the horse show competition and the medal
  finals at Ernie Howlett Park. She shared that there is a possibility that the
  assignment of the medal finals could go out to bid soon and that other horse show
  managers would be interested in bidding. Ms. Gibson stated that everything should
  be done to keep the medal finals at Ernie Howlett Park.
  Ms. Gibson stated that the cost of the Western Blend is a lot less expensive than
  the regular GGT footing but that she needs to get more information in order to say
  how much less in response to MEMBER HARIK. MEMBER HARIK noted the quote
  provided did not list the type of footing to be used. Ms. Gibson acknowledged that
  and stated that the quote also lists decomposed granite (DG) to level the base but
  she did not believe that would be necessary to which Superintendent Goldsmith
  agreed. Ms. Rowe stated that removing the DG from the quote could significantly
  lower the cost of the project. MEMBER HARIK asked if lunging and turnouts would
  still be possible as that is what she mainly sees the community members using
  that arena for to which Gibson responded affirmatively.
  MEMBER ROBINSON asked how important the medal classes are to the horse
  show. Ms. Gibson responded that losing the medal classes would end the
  Portuguese Bend Horse Show. Ms. Gibson shared that the medal finals go out to
  bid by the PCHA and that the PBNHS has had these medal finals since at least
  1985. MEMBER ROBINSON asked what other groups might bid and where the
  medal finals could possibly go. Ms. Gibson stated there is new management at the
  Del Mar Show Park, adding that PBNHS wants to attract competitors to come not
  only with their finalists but to bring others to show.
  MEMBER SILVANO asked for clarification regarding monies raised only being able
  to go towards programs for the Children’s hospital and if the PBNHS would be
  willing to share the cost. Ms. Rowe stated that if it came down to it and there was
  a way to partner with the City, they would have to fundraise outside of their
  organization, potentially with pledges from their members that would go straight to
  the City. MEMBER SILVANO noted that could be done through the Pepper Tree
  Foundation as a charitable donation.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 23, 2023
  3
   MEMBER NILSEN asked if pledges would be through potential fundraisers. Ms.
  Rowe stated that it would have to be through unofficial requests, adding that they
  would not want to fully fund the project since it is a public facility.
  MEMBER SHINN stated that she is in favor of trying to develop a plan that benefits
  all parties.
  MEMBER GRIGGS stated that new footing is needed in that arena and would like
  to see an all-weather type of footing that could also work for PBNHS.
  MEMBER ROBINSON asked how soon this would need to happen. CHAIR
  SCHMITZ noted that the budget has been set for the current fiscal year so this
  would go to the budget planning session in March. CHAIR SCHMITZ stated this
  project would need to be done before the next PBNHS event, September 9, in
  response to MEMBER ROBINSON.
  Pam Schachter, audience member, asked if the current footing had resale value
  or could be utilized in other areas if removed. Superintendent Goldsmith
  responded that it would not have any resale value, but could be utilized in other
  areas, i.e. the round pens.
  Superintendent Goldsmith recommended the project be done a month prior to the
  show to allow the footing to settle. ACM Davis noted that the project could be done
  in two weeks, making it feasible to budget and plan to have done in time for the
  show.
  Rachel Dwyer, audience member, stated that money should be allocated to arenas
  that are top of the list such as Dapplegray and that the facilities that are being used
  on a daily basis should be considered.
  CHAIR SCHMITZ explained the process for budgeting and funding projects.
  Superintendent Goldsmith shared that the Chandler Arena renovation was done
  in-house without specialty equipment leading to a longer timeline. He added that
  Dapplegray arena replenishment is budgeted, and material will be added to those
  arenas but there have been delays due to weather in response to Ms. Dwyer.
  Ms. Gibson stated that the project could be done in a timely manner adding that
  they plan to secure a professional company to complete the work.
  MEMBER SHINN stated that she liked the idea of the Western Blend and believed
  it should be a permanent installation of the footing. She added that the City should
  consider covering the cost since the PBNHS only takes place once a year.
  MEMBER SILVANO stated that she believed it should be a joint effort since it
  would be for the PBNHS show and did not feel that the City should be fully
  responsible for making the arena show quality. She added that good footing is
  needed in the rings but that it should be a collaborative effort.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 23, 2023
  4
   MEMBER CIAROLLA stated that she agreed with MEMBER SILVANO, adding that
  fundraising should be implemented with social media outreach to try to raise funds
  for the project given the benefits and that accurate quotes are needed.
  MEMBER BRTIS stated that the renovation needs to be done and that she does
  not like the current footing. She added that she is unsure how to fund it as it
  involves a charitable event and whether they can help but that it needs to be done.
  MEMBER NILSEN agreed that the renovation needs to be done and stated that
  keeping the PBNHS in the community is very important. She added that as an
  equestrian community at large, PBNHS is probably the community’s largest public
  facing equestrian event. MEMBER NILSEN stated that she agreed that the arena
  footing needs to be fixed and is very supportive of this, adding that she is
  supportive of finding a way to jointly share the costs of the project.
  MEMBER HARIK stated that she agreed with MEMBER SILVANO’S comments.
  MEMBER ROBINSON stated that she agreed and that having the PBNHS at Ernie
  Howlett Park is important to the community. She added that fundraising ideas can
  be generated to help fund the project.
  CHAIR SCHMITZ restated areas of consensus amongst the Committee which
  included the importance of the show to the community, a desire to learn more about
  the costs, the timeline, and what it is going to take to execute, and looking for
  collaborative fundraising to pay for the project.
  MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER BRTIS to:
  DIRECT STAFF TO RETURN WITH MORE INFORMATION REGARDING
  COSTS, TIMELINE, AND STEPS NEEDED TO PROCEED WITH THE
  PROJECT.
  AYES: Brtis, Ciarolla, Griggs, Nilsen, Shinn, Silvano, Robinson, Harik, and Schmitz
  ABSENT: Martin and Schachter

  The motion carried.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a verbal overview of the second
  Portuguese Bend National Horse Show (PBNHS) request per written report.

  MEMBER GRIGGS stated the turnout area would be lost if the arenas were
  combined and asked if the soft removable fencing that would divide the arena
  would be placed in a way where you can turn a horse out. Superintendent
  Goldsmith stated that turnouts, and likely lunging, would not be allowed in an arena
  that large because a horse could pick up a lot of speed in and cause damage to
  the arena when stopping. MEMBER GRIGGS stated that she rides in multi-use
  arenas with dressage courts and oftentimes dressage courts are not kept in proper
  order and asked if that would be an issue. Superintendent Goldsmith responded
  that whether or not a court is kept in there at all times would have to be determined.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 23, 2023
  5
   He explained that arena servicing is done on Mondays and Thursdays and the
  court does not come out often as the City has public arenas and is not a show
  facility. Superintendent Goldsmith added that City is unable to remove and replace
  the dressage court frequently.

  MEMBER GRIGGS asked if the arena by the maintenance yard could be
  refurbished with higher fencing so it can be used for turnouts. Superintendent
  Goldsmith shared that the fencing is the same height in that arena as the others
  but appears lower due to the elevation of the arena.

  ACM Davis noted that if the renovation were approved, part of the research would
  include looking to see if anything else additional would be needed for existing
  arenas.

  MEMBER SHINN asked if the Western Blend footing would be put in the Arenas 3
  and 4. Ms. Gibson stated the quote includes the Ebb and Flow Blend. CHAIR
  SCMITZ noted that the quote is unclear with regards to the footing. Ms. Gibson
  stated that she would provide a revised quote with a breakdown.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that dressage courts could be placed in the
  renovated ring in response to MEMBER CIAROLLA.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that it is unknown whether the dressage courts
  would be kept in the ring at all times in response to MEMBER BRTIS.

  MEMBER ROBINSON inquired about the purpose of combining Arenas 3 and 4.
  Ms. Gibson explained the need for a two-ring horse show for timing and to hold all
  the medal classes. Ms. Gibson stated combining the arenas would give extra
  footage on the backend and on the sides that would allow for a year-round
  dressage court.

  Ms. Gibson explained that the dressage arena works as one warm-up ring and the
  turnout is used as the second warm-up ring but does not work well. She explained
  that PBNHS is losing competitors because of the hard warm-up ring and stated
  that that it appears as if you could make it bigger than just the turnout and gain
  extra footage on the back ends and on the side. Ms. Gibson stated you could have
  one dressage court in there year-round and could potentially have a second
  smaller dressage court too and keep half of the arena empty for lessons until it is
  needed for the horse show.

  Ms. Gibson stated there is space, which gives the dressage community room to
  do the warm up and go around the dressage court before you enter the dressage
  court plus extra warm-up space on the other side, where again a second smaller
  dressage court could be added, enhancing what exists.

  Discussion ensued between Ms. Gibson and Ms. Dwyer about organizing and
  setting up dressage courts.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 23, 2023
  6
   Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the City’s arenas are public arenas
  maintained by City staff and that pulling the dressage court out and putting it back
  in requires a lot more maintenance than can be managed by the City. He added
  that when servicing that arena, the sand gets built up around the dressage court
  and if you have a large arena the surface will become uneven over time.

  Superintendent Goldsmith shared that PBNHS suggested potential servicing of the
  arenas an extra four times per year. Ms. Rowe stated their goal would be to have
  it serviced by the footing specialist before the show in August but could not speak
  on the idea of quarterly service.

  Ms. Schachter shared that the idea of merging the arenas was first proposed in
  2010 when she was with Las Amigas Horse Show and that David Schmutz of the
  California Dressage Society (CDS) assessed the site in consideration for
  recognized dressage shows. She stated that it was determined there was not
  enough space around the arena to prepare before entering, stating it needed to be
  wider. Ms. Schachter stated that to have enough classes you need to have two
  rings going if you do not have the circumference space needed to warm up. She
  added that CDS held shows at Ernie Howlett Park in the past but that there have
  not been any rated dressage shows for a number of years. Ms. Schachter stated
  that as it would be another incentive to be able to have shows at Ernie Howlett
  Park if there were a big enough arena in terms of circumference, adding that this
  would be an enhancement not meant to take anything away.

  Louise Koch, audience member, expressed excitement about the proposal for
  Arena 2 but concern regarding the proposal to combine Arenas 3 and 4 and agreed
  with many that it will not benefit the dressage community enough to offset potential
  concerns. She stated that the low railing used around dressage court is necessary
  but room to go around the court for a regular dressage show is not needed. She
  also shared that lunging would be tough as there is sometimes a line of riders
  waiting up to 30 minutes to lunge. She stated that if PBNHS feels the footing is too
  deep for jumpers, maybe more could be put in the dressage arena, explaining that
  there is a lack of spring in the current footing. Ms. Koch stated the dressage arena
  is the only regulation ring the community has.

  Angela Hronco, audience member, stated opposition explaining that her concern
  is the day-to-day use of those who turnout in that arena.

  Nancy Michalski, audience member, stated opposition to the proposal explaining
  that she uses Ernie Howlett Park two to three days per week. Ms. Gibson
  responded to Ms. Michalski’s question that the combined ring could be either a
  double warm up ring with dividers only put up for the horse show or in a perfect
  world it could be the main arena for the show. Ms. Michalski stated that she would
  be supportive of changing Arena 3 but combining it with Arena 4 would result in
  the dressage community losing the only arena they have to train and practice in.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith stated that when servicing the dressage
  arena, the sand builds up around the dressage court, so there would be a learning

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 23, 2023
  7
   curve as it is unknown how frequently the court could be pulled out. He furthered
  that when the sand gets built up it could eventually make the arena surface uneven.

  Ms. Michalski asked the Committee not to make a decision that would take away
  the ability of daily users to have a place to practice their sport in the hopes of
  potential dressage shows in the future.

  Valerie Goodman, audience member, thanked Superintendent Goldsmith and the
  Maintenance staff for their diligence in servicing the arenas. She stated she had
  won multiple awards and attributed her success to being able to train at Ernie
  Howlett Park. She shared information regarding her involvement with the Palos
  Verdes Dressage Chapter and stated that they are known statewide as the
  education chapter having brought in internationally renowned clinicians to Ernie
  Howlett Park. Ms. Goodman stated she is concerned about combining Arenas 3
  and 4 because the dressage court is portable, and people would likely put jumps
  in the arena or there would be schooling and riding, making it difficult to have an
  exclusive dressage area for training. Ms. Goodman asked the Committee to
  consider the pros and cons of combining the arenas and asked that the dressage
  arena not be eliminated.

  Ms. Dwyer shared that she is a dressage rider and a jumper rider and agrees that
  those are not suitable warm-up arenas. She stated that the most important thing
  for the dressage riders is having a dressage arena that is well-maintained to
  continue to train. She stated that it would be possible if it could be guaranteed that
  the dressage court will be put up and maintained daily, adding that her biggest
  concern is that the dressage arena is the only one on the Peninsula and most of
  the people she sees going to Ernie Howlett Park are dressage riders.

  Ms. Koch asked if it would help if Arena 3 were made bigger and the footing was
  changed. Ms. Gibson responded that it might.

  Audience Member Lisa Baldwin shared her concern about having different levels
  of riders in the same ring if combined. Discussion ensued regarding potential
  solutions and alternatives amongst the audience.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ closed the open comment session and opened it up to the
  Committee for questions and comments.

  MEMBER ROBINSON stated that the cost of $500,000 is an issue but expressed
  support for potential improvements to Arena 3 to improve the footing and help
  PBNHS.

  MEMBER HARIK reiterated the concern related to the $500,000 cost, adding that
  a large part of the community does not want the renovation and that Arena 3 needs
  improvement.

  MEMBER NILSEN agreed the cost is expensive and stated that the Committee
  would need to understand what pledge opportunities and cost sharing is available

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 23, 2023
  8
   from PCCH. She expressed support for PCCH and stated she does not show at
  PBNHS and thinks having horse shows is very important for the equestrian
  community. MEMBER NILSEN added that the cost is a concern but is interested
  in exploring this idea further.

  MEMBER BRTIS thinks that Arena 3 needs addressed but could not condone
  taking down the only dressage arena in the City because people need a place to
  practice.

  MEMBER CIAROLLA asked if Arena 2 is big enough to be turned into a dressage
  arena since the footing is being changed and then combine 3 and 4.
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that Arena 2 is larger than the existing
  dressage arena. MEMBER SILVANO stated that it would no longer be arenas for
  turnouts as 2 and 3 would not be useable. She added that many go to Ernie Howlett
  Park to turnout and while it is a great idea, a solution would be needed to provide
  for turnouts.

  MEMBER HARIK stated that a larger arena for dressage could attract more people
  to enter it for non-dressage uses such as lunging as there would be nowhere to
  lunge.

  MEMBER SILVANO stated the need to protect the dressage space but also protect
  the turnout space.

  MEMBER SILVANO responded that there is no available space for a round pen in
  response to MEMBER NILSEN.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the barns are used for the PBNHS as well
  as for clinics and other equestrian activities and the cost of a ten-stall portable barn
  costs $10,000 in response to MEMBER SHINN.

  MEMBER SHINN stated she is in favor of further research as well seeing what
  could be done for Arena 3, adding that she wants the PBNHS to continue at Ernie
  Howlett Park and proposed that the arena could be made bigger and the dressage
  arena left as is. MEMBER SHINN shared that she would like to see this item
  agendized for the next meeting so that ideas and solutions can be developed.

  MEMBER GRIGGS shared that she used to be a hunter jumper rider and that she
  used Arena 3 for warming up and liked it. She stated that she would like the
  dressage court to stay the same with Arena 3 footing changed and potentially
  widened, adding that she would not want a turn out arena taken away.

  Superintendent Goldsmith noted that widening of the arenas would result in
  doubling the cost of estimate due to the underground utilities adding that it is more
  feasible to get rid of the 15 feet in the center and make one large arena rather than
  going out.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 23, 2023
  9
   CHAIR SCHMITZ restated areas of consensus which included a change to the
  footing in Arena 3, the estimated cost to combine or widen the arenas not being
  realistic, and a proposal to keep this item open to the next meeting to allow for
  more information about what is feasible and what could be explored. The matter
  was continued to the next meeting.

  ACM Davis asked for clarification if the direction was to continue the matter in order
  to solely consider improvements to Arena 3 or if the direction was to look at Arena
  3 in addition to combining the arenas. It was clarified that staff would continue to
  research the option of combining the arenas and also look at options to improve
  Arena 3.

B.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUE LOG
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  HORSE TRAINER LIST (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas reported that four trainers had renewed
  their licenses and that the due date was approaching. She added that it is typical
  to only have a small number of trainers renewed by that point but shared that staff
  would be sending out another reminder to renew and share that there are late fees
  for those who renew after January 31st. Supervisor Pinuelas also reported that
  trainers can renew their licenses online, by mail, by email, and by phone.

7.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  MEMBER GRIGGS thanked Superintendent Goldsmith for work done to get a
  fallen tree removed from a trail quickly and efficiently. MEMBER GRIGGS reported
  that after the storm, on Ferncreek Trail, there was an area where the footing
  seemed to be washing away and narrowing and asked if rocks could be placed
  over there. MEMBER GRIGGS also reported that there is a home under
  construction on the same trail where they are digging into the hillside and dumping
  the dirt onto the trail. MEMBER GRIGGS also stated that while at Ernie Howlett
  Park she witnessed a Bennett Landscape employee drive through the barn at high-
  speed causing damage to the top of the barn as equipment attached to the truck
  hit the roof as he drove through the barn.

B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

8.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A.  AMBASSADOR PROGRAM

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 23, 2023
  10
   NONE.

9.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the Equestrian Committee meeting at 8:50 p.m. to the
  next meeting scheduled to be held on Monday, March 27, 2023, at 7:00 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  __________________________
  Rosa Pinuelas  Velveth Schmitz, Chair
  Community Services Supervisor

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
JANUARY 23, 2023
  11
